questions.q: Why is `gs.error('Error occurred')` considered a common and costly mistake in integration scripts?
options: It carries no identifying context — no status code, no record, no parameter — so the first hour of troubleshooting becomes reconstructing information logging could have captured for free
ServiceNow does not allow gs.error() to be called inside a catch block
It causes the integration to retry automatically three times
gs.error() messages are deleted from the system log after one hour
questions.explain: A vague message tells the person troubleshooting later almost nothing about which call, which record, or what status code was involved.

questions.q: What are the three checkpoints this lesson recommends logging at in an integration script?
options: Before sending the request, after receiving the response, and when an error occurs
Only when the script starts and only when the script ends
Only inside catch blocks, never on a successful call
Every single line of the script, regardless of what it does
questions.explain: Those three points give visibility into in-progress runs, confirm successful runs happened, and capture detail exactly when something goes wrong.

questions.q: Look at this call: `gs.error('WeatherAPI call failed for city {0}: HTTP {1} - body: {2}', city, statusCode, response.getBody());`. What does the `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` syntax do?
options: Marks placeholders in the message template that get filled in order by the arguments that follow
Marks positions where the script should insert a retry attempt
Causes the log entry to be written three separate times
Tells gs.error() to suppress the message unless debug mode is on
questions.explain: gs.info/warn/error support a message template with numbered placeholders filled in order by the trailing arguments — real, supported syntax.

questions.q: If a weather integration starts failing for one specific city but not others, why does structured logging (city, status code, timestamp) resolve this faster than vague logging?
options: The log itself can be filtered by city and read for status code and timing, instead of requiring the integration to be re-run just to see what happens
Structured logging automatically fixes the integration without any further investigation
Vague logging and structured logging take the same amount of time to troubleshoot
Structured logging prevents the external API from ever returning an error again
questions.explain: Specific, filterable values in the log let you answer "is it just this city, and since when" directly from the log, not from guesswork.

questions.q: What is IntegrationHub's execution log, and when is it the first place to look?
options: A run-by-run record of a spoke or custom action's inputs, steps, and outputs — the first place to check when a custom spoke action fails, before digging into your own gs.* output
A record of every REST Message record ever created in the instance
A list of every user who has ever logged into ServiceNow
A setting that disables gs.error() calls for performance reasons
questions.explain: The execution log is conceptually the same idea as the Flow execution log from Course 4 — it shows which step in the action's sequence a failed run actually reached.
